intent: Isolate card authorization behind one container so the shop never holds card data, and make the API -> PSP boundary visible in the checkout view.

constraints.statement: Card data MUST NOT be stored, logged or modelled inside the shop; only an authorization result crosses the adapter boundary.

evidence.note: Adapter fixture: authorization call and result mapping. Presence is not proof it runs.
Executable fixture test; execution is recorded separately from this structural check.

alternatives.title: Call the PSP directly from shop.api
alternatives.tradeoff: No new container to operate, but card scope, PSP retries and PCI boundaries land inside the request path; a PSP outage becomes a checkout outage.

alternatives.title: Sidecar proxy next to shop.api
alternatives.tradeoff: Keeps the API code clean, but the boundary is a deployment detail the C4 model cannot express, so reviewers would not see it.

alternatives.title: Payment adapter container (chosen)
alternatives.tradeoff: One more unit to deploy and monitor; buys an explicit, reviewable boundary and a separate place to gate card scope.

rationale: Authorization is independently deployable and independently failing, which is the C4 container criterion. The adapter is the only element allowed to speak to the PSP.
openQuestions: Which PSP contract version is pinned, and who rotates the merchant credential?
Does the adapter store idempotency keys, or is replay protection the API's job?
